title: Fatehpuri Masjid Delhi – History, Timings, Nearest Metro & Travel Guide
content:
Fatehpuri Masjid - Delhi,

Fatehpuri Masjid is one of the most beautiful Mughal-era mosques located at the western end of Chandni Chowk in Old Delhi. Built in 1650 by Fatehpuri Begum, one of the wives of Emperor Shah Jahan, the mosque is an important symbol of Delhi’s rich history and culture.

Constructed using red sandstone, the mosque features a large central dome and spacious courtyards that can hold hundreds of worshippers. The peaceful interiors and the spiritual aura provide a calming break from the busy markets outside.

Special Highlight: On Fridays and during major festivals like Eid, the mosque is filled with thousands of devotees, creating a powerful and spiritual atmosphere. The lively Chandni Chowk bazaar around the mosque adds to the cultural experience, making it a must-visit for history lovers and travelers alike.

Best Time to Visit: Fatehpuri Masjid can be visited throughout the year, but the best time is from October to March, when the weather is cooler and perfect for exploring both the mosque and the surrounding markets.

How to Reach Fatehpuri Masjid:

  • Nearest Metro Station: Chandni Chowk (Yellow Line). From there, it’s a short walk or rickshaw ride through the busy market lanes.
  • By Road: The mosque is easily accessible by auto-rickshaws and cabs. Parking is limited in Chandni Chowk, so public transport is the best option.
  • Nearby Attractions: Red Fort, Jama Masjid, and Khari Baoli Spice Market are all close by.

Visitor Information:

  • Timings: Open daily from 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM.
  • Entry Fee: Free for all visitors.
  • Dress Code: Modest clothing is recommended, and head covering is advised while entering the mosque.

Travel Tip: Visit early in the morning before the markets open—you’ll experience the mosque’s serene side without the hustle of Chandni Chowk.
excerpt: Fatehpuri Masjid in Chandni Chowk is a beautiful Mughal-era mosque built in 1650 by Fatehpuri Begum. Known for its stunning architecture and peaceful ambiance, it offers a serene escape in the middle of Old Delhi’s bustling markets.

faqs.question: Who built Fatehpuri Masjid and when?
faqs.answer: It was built in 1650 by Fatehpuri Begum, one of the wives of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.

faqs.question: What are the timings of Fatehpuri Masjid?
faqs.answer: The mosque is open daily from 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM.

faqs.question: Is there any entry fee for Fatehpuri Masjid?
faqs.answer: No, there is no entry fee. Visitors of all faiths are welcome to visit and explore the mosque.
